data.title: Micron or SK hynix: One AI Chip Stock Is a Bargain, the Other Too Expensive
data.description:
Micron (NASDAQ:MU) and SK hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) are selling some of the most sought-after memory chips in the AI world, yet their stocks come with different valuations. Both are benefiting from booming demand and elevated memory prices, although their strengths within the market and the prices investors pay for their earnings create a much less obvious choice between them.

Micron is the largest U.S.-based memory manufacturer, producing DRAM, NAND flash, and high-bandwidth memory, better known as HBM. That broad portfolio gives Micron exposure to smartphones, personal computers, data centers, and the advanced accelerators powering artificial intelligence workloads. SK hynix competes in many of those same markets, although its biggest advantage comes from HBM, where the South Korean chipmaker is the industry leader and a key Nvidia supplier.

American investors now have an easier way to own SK hynix following its July Nasdaq IPO. The initial enthusiasm sent SKHY substantially above its offering price, although the shares have since retreated about 29% from their post-IPO high.

Meanwhile, MU shares are up 208% this year amid soaring memory prices and exceptionally strong AI-related demand. However, the stock has become considerably more volatile since Micron reported its latest quarterly results, despite delivering another strong performance and outlook. After such a massive rally, expectations have climbed alongside the stock, leaving shareholders more sensitive to any indication that today's extraordinary memory pricing environment may eventually become less favorable.

That brings us to one investor, known by the pseudonym Alpha Analyst, who believes comparing these companies requires looking beyond their seemingly inexpensive earnings multiples. Memory manufacturers can appear particularly cheap when rising prices are sending profits toward cyclical highs, meaning low earnings multiples can sometimes give investors a misleading picture.

"A low multiple at the top is not a steal," Alpha Analyst warns, questioning whether today's elevated memory profits make traditional valuation comparisons particularly useful. In his view, Micron trading near 12 times forward earnings does not automatically make the shares inexpensive compared with the broader semiconductor industry.

SK hynix, however, gives Alpha Analyst another valuation comparison that he finds considerably more compelling. "What does work for SK hynix is that it is trading at nearly half the valuations of Micron," the investor explains.

Alpha Analyst doesn't expect investors to erase that valuation gap anytime soon, despite the improved access through Nasdaq. "I very much expect the gap to stay more sticky than my expectation suggests," the investor acknowledges, while still expecting some narrowing over a longer investment horizon.

More importantly, Alpha Analyst believes SK hynix's cheaper valuation could provide greater protection if investors eventually become less willing to pay current multiples for memory stocks. "A relative trade bullish on SK hynix versus Micron definitely appears to be better cushioned if multiples correct," the investor argues.

Valuation is not the only reason Alpha Analyst prefers SK hynix when comparing these two memory giants. The investor views SK hynix's long-term supply agreements as better positioned to capture additional pricing upside, potentially allowing the company to benefit more if memory shortages continue driving prices higher. Micron's agreements include both price ceilings and floors, providing greater certainty while potentially limiting some benefits from additional pricing increases.

Those considerations ultimately lead Alpha Analyst to rate Micron shares a Sell while giving SK hynix a Buy rating. (To watch Alpha Analyst's track record, click here)

Alpha Analyst may see a clear winner between the two, but Wall Street sees less reason to choose sides. Both Micron and SK hynix earn Strong Buy consensus ratings from analysts covering their shares. More interestingly, Wall Street sees almost identical upside ahead, with Micron's $1,560.74 average price target implying about 78% upside and SK hynix's $245.50 target pointing to a nearly identical gain. data.title: 'Playing With Fire': Investor Sounds the Alarm on Nvidia Stock
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) ended the week on a high note, climbing 2.3% on Friday and bringing its weekly gain to about 11%. Elon Musk was a key driver behind the surge after revealing that SpaceX plans to rely exclusively on Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin architecture for its AI computing needs.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

Explore NVDS for 2X short leverage on NVDA

However, investor John Engle thinks the chip giant may be taking its good fortune too far. Engle believes Nvidia is becoming financially entangled with the same ecosystem responsible for buying its products, potentially leaving the company exposed if AI spending eventually slows.

Engle's concern begins with Nvidia's growing willingness to put its balance sheet behind the AI buildout. Rather than simply selling GPUs and computing systems, Nvidia has invested in AI labs and cloud providers while exploring arrangements that can help finance infrastructure development. Engle understands the appeal while demand remains strong, but he thinks the associated risks are becoming "hard to ignore."

The trouble could arrive if the spending cycle eventually moves in the opposite direction. Nvidia could sell fewer systems while financially fragile customers struggle to meet lease, debt, or revenue obligations. Engle warns that Nvidia's efforts to support the market during the boom "could result in a double-whammy blow on the downswing."

Engle's concerns go well beyond Nvidia's growing financial involvement with its customers and partners. The investor questions whether the vast sums pouring into AI infrastructure will ultimately generate enough profits to justify continued spending. He believes the AI capex boom has moved "into the realm of irrational exuberance," while hyperscalers are approaching their cash-flow limits and shareholders are demanding greater spending discipline.

Those conditions leave Engle bracing for a potentially painful reversal in AI infrastructure spending. The investor says he "would not be at all surprised" to see a sizable spending correction, potentially developing into a "full-scale bust," within the next 12 months.

Nvidia could find itself particularly vulnerable if such a reversal eventually takes place. Engle describes the chipmaker as sitting "at the tail end of the capital-spending bullwhip," where changes in customer spending can have an outsized impact on suppliers. The operating leverage that helped Nvidia produce tremendous growth could therefore "work violently in reverse" if hyperscalers begin cutting their spending plans.

The stock's lofty valuation gives Engle another reason to worry about that possibility. He argues that Nvidia shares already assume years of heavy hyperscaler spending and durable pricing power, leaving little room for disappointment if AI investment cools.

"Nvidia's stock is not trading as if the AI bubble could burst," Engle warns. He still believes Nvidia would "probably emerge intact" from a severe spending reversal, given its technological advantages and formidable software ecosystem. However, surviving such a downturn would offer shareholders limited reassurance after potentially steep stock losses. Engle calls that prospect "cold comfort to investors buying the top," capturing why he believes Nvidia may be playing with fire.

Accordingly, the investor rates NVDA shares a Sell. (To watch Engle's track record, click here)

While Engle is clearly in the bear camp, Wall Street sees Nvidia very differently. Of the 37 analysts covering NVDA, 36 recommend buying the stock, with just one remaining on the sidelines. That gives Nvidia a Strong Buy consensus, while the $308.69 average price target points to about 38% upside from current levels. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: SpaceX Short Sellers Are Getting Smashed — Here's What J.P. Morgan Sees Next
data.description:
SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) short sellers have suddenly found themselves on the wrong side of an explosive rebound. The shares have jumped about 23% over the past two trading sessions after Thursday's closely watched lockup expiration failed to produce the massive selloff many had feared.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

High conviction on SPCX? Try Tradr's SPCM or SPCG

Short interest had climbed to 219.3 million shares by July 29, representing about $24.6 billion worth of bearish bets heading into the event. With more than 900 million restricted shares becoming eligible for trading Thursday, short sellers had reason to expect additional supply would weigh heavily on the stock. That selling wave, however, didn't arrive.

With SpaceX shares moving substantially higher instead, short sellers closing positions can add further buying to the market, creating the conditions for a short squeeze. The question now is whether that squeeze has more room to run as shareholders reconsider SpaceX's longer-term growth prospects.

J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth certainly sees plenty to like after reviewing the company's latest earnings.

"SPCX continues to benefit from extreme vertical integration," Anmuth writes, while arguing that "the pace of change in AI is incredibly fast." That combination matters as SpaceX applies engineering expertise developed through rockets and satellites toward expanding its data-center infrastructure at an aggressive pace.

Anmuth now believes the opportunity surrounding AI computing could arrive much sooner than his previous forecasts suggested. SpaceX expects computing capacity to rise from more than two gigawatts this year toward five to ten gigawatts during 2027, while stronger pricing could further improve the economics surrounding that capacity.

The implications could be substantial if SpaceX delivers anywhere near those expectations. Anmuth believes greater capacity and higher monetization "suggests that SPCX could pull forward previously modeled AI revenue for 2028 of $100B+ to 2027." That represents a meaningful acceleration for a business that has become central to J.P. Morgan's long-term outlook for SpaceX.

The spending required to reach those levels remains immense, although Anmuth sees encouraging economics behind those investments. SpaceX is currently generating payback on compute investments in around one year or less, which the analyst believes is "likely much faster than the industry." That helps explain why Anmuth is willing to look beyond the immense capital expenditures required during the coming years.

Meanwhile, Starship gives Anmuth another reason to remain optimistic about SpaceX's broader growth prospects. Management "appears more confident that it has solved the heat shield problem," while Anmuth describes Starship as "the key enabler for all other parts of the business."

Those developments prompted Anmuth to raise his 2026 revenue estimate by 14% to $47 billion while lifting his 2027 projection by 64% to $123 billion, with AI computing accounting for much of those increases.

Accordingly, Anmuth assigns SpaceX shares an Overweight (i.e., Buy) rating, while his $240 price target implies an 80% upside from current levels. (To watch Anmuth's track record, click here)

data.title: SpaceX's $60B Cursor Deal Could Close Next Week… But the Cursor Brand May Disappear
data.description:
Aerospace company SpaceX (SPCX) could complete its $60 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor as soon as the end of next week, according to The Information. The deal is expected to close by the end of August at the latest, depending on final regulatory approvals. At the same time, Cursor employees were told that the company's brand may slowly disappear from future products, with some upcoming tools potentially using SpaceX's Grok name instead.

High conviction SPCX bulls now have this Tradr ETF

One example is Cursor's planned general-purpose AI agent, currently known internally as "Sand." That product could eventually launch as "Grok Bot," although no final decision has been made. Existing products, including the popular Cursor coding assistant, are not expected to be renamed right away. Another option being discussed is creating an entirely new brand rather than using Grok.

Regardless, once the deal closes, Cursor employees are expected to move into SpaceX's internal systems and reporting structure within days. The two companies are already working closely together after announcing an AI partnership in April. That agreement gave Cursor access to SpaceX's computing infrastructure while allowing the companies to develop AI models together.

Cursor Could Help Grok Gain More Traction

The acquisition could be especially important for SpaceX's growing AI business. Indeed, Cursor brings enterprise customers and valuable coding data, which could help Grok gain more traction with businesses. Recently, SpaceX reported $2.6 billion of AI revenue in the second quarter, but it also spent heavily on data centers, with total capital expenditures reaching $18.4 billion.

Nevertheless, SpaceX has said that it expects companywide revenue to reach a $100 billion annualized pace by December, including Cursor, although management still expects selling cloud-computing capacity to remain the biggest driver of that target.

data.title: Stock Market Today: SPY, QQQ Rally after Disappointing Jobs Report Reshapes Rate Expectations
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ) closed higher on Friday after a weaker-than-expected jobs report lowered interest rate hike odds.

News That Moved the Stock Market Today

  • Nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, far below the expected 80,000 increase. In addition, May and June payrolls were revised down by a combined 103,000.
  • The labor force participation rate dropped to 61.4%, marking its lowest level since February 2021. That contributed to the unemployment rate falling to 4.1% from 4.2% in June. 
  • However, the disappointing data came with a silver lining, at least for stocks. With a weaker labor market, the Fed is less inclined to hike rates. That's because lower rates support employment by reducing borrowing costs and encouraging businesses to invest and hire.
  • Following the report, the odds of a rate hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting fell to 43.9% from 55%, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
  •  Citi analyst Atif Malik slashed his Micron (MU) price target to $1,150 from $1,400. Malik expects NAND and DRAM price growth to decelerate in the next four quarters before peaking in the second quarter of 2027.
  • Cloudflare (NET) rallied to an all-time high after its second-quarter results beat on both revenue and adjusted EPS.
  • On the other hand, Trade Desk (TTD) plummeted after publishing its earnings, sending its year-to-date loss to 63%.
  • SpaceX (SPCX) rallied following its first lock-up expiration on Thursday when over 900 million shares became available.

data.title: Does the U.K. Deal Mean Trouble? Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Gains Regardless
data.description:
When news emerged that the United Kingdom's various regulators had signed off on entertainment giant Paramount Skydance's (PSKY) merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), some thought it was a good sign. But others think it may be the beginning of the end for the deal after all. Investors seemed optimistic, though, and gave Paramount shares an extra 2% in the closing minutes of Friday's trading.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

When the Competition and Markets Authority let the deal go through, some figured that this was one more nail in the coffin of the states' case. After all, when this many markets are letting the deal go through, even with some concessions and assurances, suggesting that the deal is somehow a competition-killer looks like a long shot. But some believe that it is those very same concessions that give the states' argument against the deal weight.

Basically, the idea that Paramount's deal requires concessions to go through in the U.K., where its market share is significantly lower than it is in the United States, suggests that the deal is much more dangerous in a market where Paramount's market share is much higher and the market more concentrated. But given that the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) already allowed the deal through, that argument loses some weight.

Paramount+ Outage

And right at the same time that Paramount is trying to get its deal through, its flagship streaming operation, Paramount+, suffered an outage. Starting from around nine this morning, and continuing until about noon, users reported errors with video streaming. Some also found problems with the app itself, suggesting that the problem was more widespread than some might have expected.

But based on further information, the problem seemed mostly resolved by early afternoon, with only a comparative handful of issues reported after the largest number of reports. Any outage is a bad one when it comes to streaming services, but it also represents an opportunity for above-and-beyond customer service. If Paramount is quick to offer outage credits here, then it might keep some users in the fold, even as users regularly switch from one provider to another.

data.title: Burger King (QSR) Overtakes Wendy's to Become Second-Largest U.S. Burger Chain
data.description:
Burger King, owned by Restaurant Brands International (QSR), has surpassed Wendy's (WEN) to become the second-largest burger chain in America.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Burger King is now second only to McDonald's (MCD) when it comes to systemwide sales among burger restaurant chains in the U.S. Burger King had fallen out of second place and been overtaken by Wendy's six years ago amid declining sales at its U.S. restaurants.

However, Restaurant Brands International has invested heavily in a multi-year turnaround strategy at Burger King, and managed to revive the chain's fortunes, as evidenced by the company's recently reported second-quarter financial results.

The Revival of Burger King

Restaurant Brands reported strong second-quarter financial results due largely to a recovery in the Burger King chain. The Toronto-based company, which also owns Tim Hortons and Popeyes, said Burger King's U.S. same-store sales rose 8.5% year-over-year in Q2. International Burger King restaurants saw same-store sales growth of 5.4% during the quarter.

The growth comes after the burger chain underwent restaurant renovations and launched a new marketing campaign. "Burger King's performance is a great example of what's possible when you invest in the fundamentals and execute well," said Restaurant Brands CEO Josh Kobza in the company's earnings statement.

News that Burger King has moved into second place among U.S. burger chains also comes on the same day that Wendy's reported sluggish sales and announced that it is cutting its dividend in half. Management at Wendy's cited declining customer traffic and shrinking franchisee profits reasons for its poor results and the dividend cut. Wendy's sales were up only 1% from a year ago in the second quarter.

Restaurant Brands International's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating among 14 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 10 Buy and four Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average QSR price target of $85.64 implies 16% upside from current levels.
